approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs. It keeps the highest-scoring survivors, favors their upper score bands when choosing parents, and generates offspring with mutation chains and connected-fragment crossover. Accepted offspring can become later parents. Every accepted score also enters a complete archive used by a count-fingerprint Gaussian process to select each evaluation batch from a larger fresh candidate pool through correlated posterior draws. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled, while ordinary graph edits, stable molecular identity checks, duplicate rejection and bounded fallbacks remain active.
approach.novelty: Test one registered combination linking survivor retention to its breeding consumer: keep the incumbent and newest other live records, then draw parents uniformly from every eligible live survivor. The recency-only sibling stored extra records that never bred; the uniform-live sibling used otherwise unsupported parents under greedy retention. Both lowered the mean. This exact joint implementation supplies the missing fourth treatment, follows protected records into actual use and scored descendants, and measures the total interaction. It differs from recent-score-tie priority and core-based retention, and makes no separate component-benefit or performance-rescue claim.

hypothesis: Jointly replace nonincumbent greedy survivor membership with the exact incumbent-preserving newest-serial rule from n-8fa256ded991 and replace rank-preferred live-parent choice with the exact all-eligible-live uniform law from n-a56491c332aa, on the single code Parent n-62daf219c70a, to connect directly protected survivors to their breeding consumer.

finding_summary.headline: Protected records reached scored offspring, but the joint mean fell and the interaction was negative
finding_summary.insights:
Changing the consumer removed the storage-without-use obstruction observed with recency alone, but making protected alternatives breed did not recover endpoint performance. This is a resolved negative result for the exact joint intervention and its matched-panel interaction. It does not assign the loss to either component separately or settle the value of the wider graph-evolution foundation. The original losses from both single controls remain.

Participation and productive search separated sharply: the joint run produced 1,060 strict generating-parent wins versus 629 for the Parent, against weaker generating parents, while sequential incumbent advances fell from 258 to 201. Protected ancestry reached 525 accepted records and twelve incumbent advances, but only one final leader; overlapping ancestry is not proof that a retained structure mediated the endpoint. More perceived molecular cores likewise did not establish useful chemical diversity: the molecular assessment found 2,005 typed and 1,327 generic cores versus 1,850 and 1,117 for the Parent, alongside 299 tiny products versus 99 and continuing unusual ring bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. Recognizable cyclic amines and carbonyl frameworks remain counterexamples to treating every product as implausible. Neither core counts nor founder reachability measures retained atoms or synthetic feasibility.

The fixed combination has an exposed, complete answer without rescue tuning. Why particular trajectories lose, which chemistry would be useful, and how the broader foundation contributes remain open; this shared-Parent panel supplies neither independent replication nor reliability beyond the issued seeds.
finding_summary.results:
The access mechanism worked. Of 196 records retained against a local greedy eviction, 182 reached a later live population and all 182 were subsequently sampled, in 3,736 parent draws. The other 14 had no later opportunity. Those parents produced 155 accepted offspring, of which 151 later bred. Only two immediately advanced the incumbent. The stricter group still directly protected at the consumed retention contest produced 61 accepted offspring and no immediate incumbent gains. In median_2 seed 2, protected parents were drawn 140 times but produced no accepted offspring. All fifteen joint task runs completed.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.530508, a paired loss of 0.065161. All three seed macros and all five task means declined; three of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. The joint mean was also 0.053355 below recency alone and 0.019163 below uniform-live sampling alone. The four-treatment interaction, joint minus recency minus uniform plus the Parent, was −0.007357, beyond the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Its seed values were +0.025676, −0.057736 and +0.009990, with population deviation 0.036194, so the negative mean does not describe every seed.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and aryl-amine families persist, alongside more tiny fragments, unusual ring bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character:
All supplied Child and published Parent trajectories were read for all five objectives and Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. The brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with all seeds matched and no profile mismatches. The indexed published recency-only n-8fa256ded991 and uniform-live-only n-a56491c332aa trajectories were also read descriptively: 60 files and 18,000 observations in total, with no missing paths. Each node contributes 4,500 observations, including 4,350 optimizer products and 150 fixed initial records; each task contributes 870 optimizer products. No task was omitted. Only accepted evaluated products and initial observations are visible in these trajectories; unselected candidate pools have no invented scores or inferred chemistry coverage. The digest final_molecules are the tail of seed 2, not every seed's best molecule. All seed leaders and selected low and final examples below come from the full trajectories. Original indexed molecular reports for the Parent and both component comparators were read to preserve the source and conditions of recurring gaps.

The Child produces recognizable annulated aryl carboxamides and ketones, azaarene/carbonyl assemblies, biaryl cyclic amines, cyclic urea/imide-like systems, fluorinated carbocycles and thiourea/hydrazone structures. Optimizer median heavy-atom counts, in fixed task order, are 24, 34, 32, 31 and 26, versus Parent 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. Across the Child, the range is one to 113 heavy atoms and the median is 28 heavy atoms with four RDKit-perceived rings. Ring and aromatic chemistry are abundant: digest ring-digit incidences range from 0.8621 to 0.9517, and aromatic-text incidences from 0.6425 to 0.9253. These are the fraction of molecule strings containing the feature, not the fraction of atoms aromatic, physical ring feasibility or scaffold counts. The chemically recognizable families and conventional cyclic-amine leaders are meaningful counterexamples to calling every output implausible. Nevertheless, reactive-looking local bonds, constrained unsaturation, complex bridges and many unspecified configurations justify questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall medicinal-chemistry quality; none is a synthesis or activity measurement.

The distinction between identities, perceived cores and ancestry matters. Over the evaluated optimizer records the Child has 4,138 distinct exact SMILES and 2,005 nonempty typed / 1,327 generic Murcko cores; Parent has 4,286 strings and 1,850 / 1,117 cores. The component comparators have 1,782 / 1,055 and 2,060 / 1,403 cores, respectively. Generic cores replace atom types and bond orders, and all core counting omits stereochemistry; empty acyclic cores are excluded. This shows substantial perceived topology variation, while recurring leading families within seeds support moderate rather than collapsed chemical diversity. It does not show independent plausible pharmacophores, useful diversity or atoms retained from a founder. Trajectory files do not map atoms or provide actual-parent ancestry; founder reachability, if supplied by a separate provenance audit, remains graph ancestry rather than conserved scaffold chemistry. No protected-record, component-activation or chemical-mediation conclusion is drawn here.

The Child includes 299 products with at most three heavy atoms, versus Parent 99, recency-only 105 and uniform-live-only 134; 425 Child products are acyclic versus Parent 129. Conversely, direct N-halogen / O-halogen / O-O bond-bearing record counts are 489 / 145 / 114 for Child, 1,042 / 278 / 273 for Parent, 897 / 456 / 319 for recency-only and 483 / 247 / 157 for uniform-live-only. These overlapping counts are whole-record occurrences, not distinct bonds or a combined quality score. Ring-triple-bond and ring-cumulated-carbon flags occur in 41 and 61 Child products, versus 17 and 42 in Parent. Fewer heteroatom-halogen flags therefore do not establish general chemical improvement. RDKit identifies possible unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,446 Child products versus 2,408 Parent products, while all Child digest stereocentre and charge-string incidences are zero. Neutral tertiary amines remain plainly present, so absence of charge notation does not mean absence of basic sites. Potential centres are structural flags, not proof of configurational stability.

The per-seed endpoint scores below are existing trajectory observations, not newly assigned scores. Their structural associations do not identify why a score changed, the objective's full desired chemistry, or separate effects of the two jointly changed decisions. The current comparison has one code Parent, and the published component trajectories remain their own adaptive histories. No additive chemical contribution, significance, unseen-seed reliability or whole-foundation value follows. Read-only CPU descriptor definitions, original trajectory hashes and all records are in .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r21-slot3-molecular/trajectory_descriptors.json and molecule_records.jsonl; describe.py reproduces them without candidate or oracle execution.

The earlier n-c55c3d520a2c source provenance is historical: its profile boundary is not converted into a matched comparison here. Current complete pairing refers specifically to n-62daf219c70a.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Protected records reached scored offspring, but the joint mean fell and the interaction was negative
finding_summary.insights:
Changing the consumer removed the storage-without-use obstruction observed with recency alone, but making protected alternatives breed did not recover endpoint performance. This is a resolved negative result for the exact joint intervention and its matched-panel interaction. It does not assign the loss to either component separately or settle the value of the wider graph-evolution foundation. The original losses from both single controls remain.

Participation and productive search separated sharply: the joint run produced 1,060 strict generating-parent wins versus 629 for the Parent, against weaker generating parents, while sequential incumbent advances fell from 258 to 201. Protected ancestry reached 525 accepted records and twelve incumbent advances, but only one final leader; overlapping ancestry is not proof that a retained structure mediated the endpoint. More perceived molecular cores likewise did not establish useful chemical diversity: the molecular assessment found 2,005 typed and 1,327 generic cores versus 1,850 and 1,117 for the Parent, alongside 299 tiny products versus 99 and continuing unusual ring bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. Recognizable cyclic amines and carbonyl frameworks remain counterexamples to treating every product as implausible. Neither core counts nor founder reachability measures retained atoms or synthetic feasibility.

The fixed combination has an exposed, complete answer without rescue tuning. Why particular trajectories lose, which chemistry would be useful, and how the broader foundation contributes remain open; this shared-Parent panel supplies neither independent replication nor reliability beyond the issued seeds.
finding_summary.results:
The access mechanism worked. Of 196 records retained against a local greedy eviction, 182 reached a later live population and all 182 were subsequently sampled, in 3,736 parent draws. The other 14 had no later opportunity. Those parents produced 155 accepted offspring, of which 151 later bred. Only two immediately advanced the incumbent. The stricter group still directly protected at the consumed retention contest produced 61 accepted offspring and no immediate incumbent gains. In median_2 seed 2, protected parents were drawn 140 times but produced no accepted offspring. All fifteen joint task runs completed.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.530508, a paired loss of 0.065161. All three seed macros and all five task means declined; three of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. The joint mean was also 0.053355 below recency alone and 0.019163 below uniform-live sampling alone. The four-treatment interaction, joint minus recency minus uniform plus the Parent, was −0.007357, beyond the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Its seed values were +0.025676, −0.057736 and +0.009990, with population deviation 0.036194, so the negative mean does not describe every seed.

finding_summary.headline: Protected records reached scored offspring, but the joint mean fell and the interaction was negative
finding_summary.insights:
Changing the consumer removed the storage-without-use obstruction observed with recency alone, but making protected alternatives breed did not recover endpoint performance. This is a resolved negative result for the exact joint intervention and its matched-panel interaction. It does not assign the loss to either component separately or settle the value of the wider graph-evolution foundation. The original losses from both single controls remain.

Participation and productive search separated sharply: the joint run produced 1,060 strict generating-parent wins versus 629 for the Parent, against weaker generating parents, while sequential incumbent advances fell from 258 to 201. Protected ancestry reached 525 accepted records and twelve incumbent advances, but only one final leader; overlapping ancestry is not proof that a retained structure mediated the endpoint. More perceived molecular cores likewise did not establish useful chemical diversity: the molecular assessment found 2,005 typed and 1,327 generic cores versus 1,850 and 1,117 for the Parent, alongside 299 tiny products versus 99 and continuing unusual ring bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. Recognizable cyclic amines and carbonyl frameworks remain counterexamples to treating every product as implausible. Neither core counts nor founder reachability measures retained atoms or synthetic feasibility.

The fixed combination has an exposed, complete answer without rescue tuning. Why particular trajectories lose, which chemistry would be useful, and how the broader foundation contributes remain open; this shared-Parent panel supplies neither independent replication nor reliability beyond the issued seeds.
finding_summary.results:
The access mechanism worked. Of 196 records retained against a local greedy eviction, 182 reached a later live population and all 182 were subsequently sampled, in 3,736 parent draws. The other 14 had no later opportunity. Those parents produced 155 accepted offspring, of which 151 later bred. Only two immediately advanced the incumbent. The stricter group still directly protected at the consumed retention contest produced 61 accepted offspring and no immediate incumbent gains. In median_2 seed 2, protected parents were drawn 140 times but produced no accepted offspring. All fifteen joint task runs completed.

Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.530508, a paired loss of 0.065161. All three seed macros and all five task means declined; three of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. The joint mean was also 0.053355 below recency alone and 0.019163 below uniform-live sampling alone. The four-treatment interaction, joint minus recency minus uniform plus the Parent, was −0.007357, beyond the registered 0.002 descriptive scale. Its seed values were +0.025676, −0.057736 and +0.009990, with population deviation 0.036194, so the negative mean does not describe every seed.

Each node contributes 4,500 observations, including 4,350 optimizer products and 150 fixed initial records; each task contributes 870 optimizer products. No task was omitted. The Child produces recognizable annulated aryl carboxamides and ketones, azaarene/carbonyl assemblies, biaryl cyclic amines, cyclic urea/imide-like systems, fluorinated carbocycles and thiourea/hydrazone structures. Optimizer median heavy-atom counts, in fixed task order, are 24, 34, 32, 31 and 26, versus Parent 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. Across the Child, the range is one to 113 heavy atoms and the median is 28 heavy atoms with four RDKit-perceived rings. Ring and aromatic chemistry are abundant: digest ring-digit incidences range from 0.8621 to 0.9517, and aromatic-text incidences from 0.6425 to 0.9253. These are the fraction of molecule strings containing the feature, not the fraction of atoms aromatic, physical ring feasibility or scaffold counts. The chemically recognizable families and conventional cyclic-amine leaders are meaningful counterexamples to calling every output implausible. Nevertheless, reactive-looking local bonds, constrained unsaturation, complex bridges and many unspecified configurations justify questionable synthetic plausibility and weak overall medicinal-chemistry quality; none is a synthesis or activity measurement.

The distinction between identities, perceived cores and ancestry matters. Over the evaluated optimizer records the Child has 4,138 distinct exact SMILES and 2,005 nonempty typed / 1,327 generic Murcko cores; Parent has 4,286 strings and 1,850 / 1,117 cores. The component comparators have 1,782 / 1,055 and 2,060 / 1,403 cores, respectively. Generic cores replace atom types and bond orders, and all core counting omits stereochemistry; empty acyclic cores are excluded. This shows substantial perceived topology variation, while recurring leading families within seeds support moderate rather than collapsed chemical diversity. It does not show independent plausible pharmacophores, useful diversity or atoms retained from a founder. Trajectory files do not map atoms or provide actual-parent ancestry; founder reachability, if supplied by a separate provenance audit, remains graph ancestry rather than conserved scaffold chemistry. No protected-record, component-activation or chemical-mediation conclusion is drawn here.

The Child includes 299 products with at most three heavy atoms, versus Parent 99, recency-only 105 and uniform-live-only 134; 425 Child products are acyclic versus Parent 129.
